description: The Space Syntax Toolkit is a QGIS plugin that runs space syntax analysis inside a GIS, acting as a front-end for the depthmapX software so that street network and visibility graph analyses can be prepared, run and mapped without leaving QGIS. It was first written by Jorge Gil at the Space Syntax Laboratory of the Bartlett, University College London, with later contributions from Space Syntax Limited staff, and adds modules for preparing and checking network data, analysing it and exploring the results. The repository holds the plugin source, documentation and a sample dataset for following the tutorials. Coverage: any city or site with a street or space layout. Access: free from the QGIS plugins manager and GitHub; version 0.3.10; needs QGIS 3.10 or later and depthmapXnet. Licence: GPL-3.0. Caveats: the last commit is from April 2024 and the mailing list has closed, so support is through issues. Simulation uses are street network integration and choice measures to estimate pedestrian movement potential in public spaces, and comparing layouts before and after changes. Related records: depthmapX, QGIS and OpenStreetMap as a street network source.
